summary.en: Coarse grind, five 60 g pours about 45 seconds apart, each after the previous has almost drained. The first 40 % of the water sets the taste, the last 60 % sets the strength.
summary.pt-BR: Moagem grossa, cinco despejos de 60 g com cerca de 45 segundos de intervalo, cada um depois que o anterior quase escoou. Os primeiros 40 % da água definem o sabor, os 60 % finais definem a intensidade.

grind.note: Philocoffea: medium-coarse to coarse; kosher-salt texture. Japanese Coffee Gear puts Kasuya's grind at 28–30 clicks on a Comandante C40, the top of that grinder's pour-over chart, so the recipe sits at the coarse edge of the V60 window (800 µm on the Honest Coffee Guide scale). Coarser than every other V60 recipe here.

temperature.note: Philocoffea (Kasuya's company) gives about 93 °C light, 88 °C medium, 83 °C dark. Hario UK and Hario Europe give 92 °C for Kasuya's own brew; Japanese Coffee Gear gives 92–94 / 88–91 / 85–88. Sources disagree by 2–3 °C per roast level; Philocoffea's values are used here.

source.title: Philocoffea: Tetsu Kasuya's 4:6 Method
source.notes: Each pour is 3 × dose and total water is 15 × dose. Adjustments: in the first 40 %, less water in pour 1 (50 + 70) gives a sweeter cup, more (70 + 50) gives a brighter one, 60 + 60 is balanced. In the last 60 %, one pour (180 g) is the lightest, two pours (90 + 90) medium, three pours (60 × 3) the strongest; Philocoffea suggests two pours for dark roasts. The 2016 competition schedule differs: 50 g, 70 g, then 60 g × 3, with pour 5 at 2:45 (Philocoffea), 2:40 (Hario UK/Europe) or 3:00 (Japanese Coffee Gear).
